title: 79 payer portals, and what each one lets you do online
summary: A matrix of 79 payer, clearinghouse, Medicare, Medicaid and UM portals, with a lamp for each transaction a provider can do online. 64 take a prior auth. The Medicare MACs do not.
body_markdown:
Ask a prior auth team how many logins they hold and the answer is usually “too many”. We counted. The[payer portal matrix](https://asteroid.ai/market-maps/payer-portals) lists 79 of them in eight groups, with a lamp for each thing you can do online.


## The seven lamps


E eligibility, A auth submission, S status, C claim entry, R remits, P appeals and attachments, N enrolment. A filled lamp means the portal does it. An empty one means phone, fax or another system.


Click a column header to require that transaction. Combine them: “auth submission and appeals online” leaves 35 portals. “Everything online” leaves 10.


## What stands out


Medicare does not take a prior auth online. All seven MAC portals light up for eligibility, status, claims, remits, appeals and enrolment, and none for auth submission. That goes through esMD, fax or the MAC’s own forms.


Fourteen payers live inside Availity. Aetna, Humana, Anthem, Molina, Florida Blue, HCSC and the rest have no portal of their own for provider work. One login, but one set of Availity quirks.


Eleven portals hold the auth decision. Seven of them, eviCore, Carelon, RadMD, Cohere, HealthHelp, TurningPoint and nH Access, take the auth and the status check and nothing else. HomeBridge also takes a claim. Provider Express, ProviderConnect and Magellan take eligibility, claims and remits too. The plan’s own portal just points there.


Pharmacy is separate. CoverMyMeds, Surescripts and the PBMs take the auth and the status, never the claim.


## Scope


The lamps show the typical scope of each portal. Plans and states carve out exceptions, and portals change. If a lamp is wrong, the “Suggest a correction” button prefills a note with the portal name.
